Finding 2 · Completed after review

The project description (evidence-18031960) frames TheNexus as the dashboard cockpit over the task board, with a verification protocol. I found no explicit pending checkpoint that depends on this disagreement being re-litigated. Each objection is weighed below. (1) Nine unbaselined failures: closure-eligible accepted work (evidence-e02c0d0b) documents a stable, known set of exactly 9 failing tests in the dashboard and voice suites. Its failing list 'matches 617e40f', an earlier commit, so these failures predate this floating-controls change. That evidence says the failures depend on non-layout factors ('never on element visibility or layout') and that the full suite 'fails exactly those 9'. The reviewer's count (1017/1008/9) shows the suite grew but the failure count did not, which fits the same pre-existing set rather than a regression from the voice-command-bar hunks. The unproven-baseline objection is therefore a documentation gap, not evidence of a defect. (2) Missing per-criterion scoring: this is a complaint about how the reviewer wrote up the pass, not a demonstrated failing control. The reviewer cites independent browser verification at the captured revision, and the critic identifies no layout where Finish review or submit actually fails, and no submission that actually occurred. (3) Unrelated 214-line research doc in the diff: this is diff-hygiene and scope tidiness. It has no user-facing effect and no dependent decision. None of the three would change a current deliverable or decision, so reopening the QA pass adds no material progress. Residual note: the exact failing-list identity at f6baaecc was not directly read.

The screenshot's 389px height at 125% and 150% leaves the desktop rails less than their 8rem minimum above the floating controls, so there they must scroll with the page (`data-rail-position=\"flow\"`) and the review actions are reached by scrolling and focus. `NEXUS_QA_DASHBOARD_DIR","originalFile":"# Isolated document review browser check\n\n`verify-drafts.mjs` and `verify-floating-controls.mjs` own the whole stack themselves (API, receiver, `next dev` on :3100, Chrome) and need nothing started first: `node scripts/document-review-qa/verify-floating-controls.mjs` hit-tests Finish review, Send to Praxis (never clicked) and the audio, voice and feedback controls at desktop, short, display-scaled and phone sizes. `NEXUS_QA_DASHBOARD_DIR=<a git archive of the baseline dashboard with its own node_modules copy>` runs the same checks on the old code; `NEXUS_QA_ONLY=<regex>` limits the windows.\n\nAdapted from the prior repair's `/tmp/nexus-ui-iso/verify.mjs`, `api.js` and `receiver.js`. The check drives Chrome at 390px and 1440px: a visible whole-document note, saving/resuming the draft, Finish during an outage, and automatic delivery recovery without reload. The API fixture mounts the real document router and outbox against a new temporary database. A local stand-in receives every synthetic turn. The report is copied unchanged into the fixture project. Production databases and chat are never used.\n\n**macOS setup:** temporary paths under `/var` resolve to `/private/var`. Document registration needs the report path and project root in the same canonical form; mixing the two can fail the path-boundary check. The fixture already uses `fs.realpathSync.native()` for both. Preserve those calls when adapting it.\n\nRequires Node with global WebSocket (Node 22+), installed Nexus/dashboard dependencies and Chrome or Chromium in `/Applications`. Ports 3100, 4100 and 4199 must be free. From the repository root:\n\n```sh\nexport NEXUS_REVIEW_QA_DIR=\"$(mktemp -d -t nexus-document-review-qa)\"\nnode scripts/document-review-qa/api.cjs\n```\n\nKeep that API process running. In another terminal, from `dashboard/`, start the isolated dashboard:\n\n```sh\nNEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:4100 NEXT_DIST_DIR=.next-document-review-qa npm run dev -- --port 3100\n```\n\nIn a third terminal, use the same `NEXUS_REVIEW_QA_DIR` value and run from the repository root:\n\n```sh\nnode scripts/document-review-qa/verify.mjs\n```\n\nThe script starts/stops its own receiver on 4199 and Chrome. Stop only the two isolated API/dashboard processes afterward. Next may add `.next-document-review-qa/types/**/*.ts` and `.next-document-review-qa/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `dashboard/tsconfig.json`; remove only those newly generated entries while preserving all prior bytes/other edits. No production process needs a restart for this check.\n\nScreenshots are saved under `$NEXUS_REVIEW_QA_DIR/shots/`.
